USA criticano i deep strikes ucraini in Russia, scontro con gli alleati europei

20261118-125640e258.caption:
Il Pentagono critica i raid ucraini in Russia, Berlino e Londra lo contestano

Secondo CNBC, il sottosegretario alla Difesa USA Elbridge Colby ha detto a Bruxelles che i "deep strike" ucraini non hanno aiutato a chiudere la guerra e avrebbero rafforzato la determinazione russa. Il ministro tedesco Boris Pistorius ha definito la critica "una cosa piuttosto stupida", il britannico Wes Streeting ha detto che non spetta agli alleati dire a Kiev come combattere. Lo scontro arriva prima del vertice di giovedì tra Trump, Putin e Xi a Shenzhen.

Gli alleati devono porre limiti alle scelte militari di Kiev?

c.titolo_copertina: Gli Stati Uniti criticano i raid ucraini in Russia, Germania e Regno Unito li difendono

slide.titolo: Colby attacca i "deep strike" di Kiev
slide.testo: Al quartier generale NATO in Belgio, il sottosegretario alla Difesa USA Elbridge Colby ha paragonato i raid ucraini in profondità in Russia a uno spettacolo. Secondo lui "non sono stati efficaci" per chiudere la guerra né per frenare le avanzate russe.

Colby cita gli attacchi a Wildberries, il più grande rivenditore online russo: colpire "infrastrutture civili" avrebbe rafforzato la determinazione russa. Kiev sostiene che i magazzini fornivano componenti militari. Wildberries e il Cremlino negano.
Secondo Colby, a ottobre le forze ucraine hanno conquistato più territorio della Russia per il secondo mese consecutivo. Gli attacchi a medio raggio con droni, ammette, sono stati "molto efficaci".
Criticare questi attacchi contro obiettivi militari strategici in Russia è una cosa piuttosto stupida, credo.
slide.autore: Boris Pistorius, ministro della Difesa tedesco

slide.testo: Il ministro della Difesa britannico Wes Streeting: "Non spetta a noi dire all'Ucraina come combattere la sua guerra". Secondo lui, i raid hanno contribuito a indebolire la macchina bellica di Putin, "guadagnando tempo e salvando vite".

slide.titolo: Colpito il ponte di Kerch, poi il vertice
slide.testo: Zelensky rivendica un'"operazione senza precedenti" con droni e missili sul ponte tra Russia e Crimea occupata, che è stato danneggiato. Mosca promette di ricostruirlo. Giovedì Trump, Putin e Xi si incontrano a Shenzhen, a margine dell'APEC.

c.perche_ti_riguarda: La divisione tra Washington ed Europa sulla strategia ucraina pesa su NATO e UE, di cui l'Italia fa parte. E i raid sulle raffinerie russe toccano l'energia: Trump li ha accusati di causare una carenza globale di gasolio.

sources.title: US hits out at Ukraine's 'deep strikes' against Russia in rift with EU over war tactics
sources.text: US hits out at Ukraine's 'deep strikes' against Russia in rift with EU over war tactics. Top US defence official Elbridge Colby criticised Ukraine's "deep strikes" against Russia Tuesday, as President Volodymyr Zelensky urged Kyiv's backers to send air defences without delay. His comments, delivered at a gathering of Ukraine's allies in Brussels, was flat out rejected by both Germany and the United Kingdom, who hit back at the Americans' suggestion. sources.title: Ukraine allies reject U.S. criticism of deep strikes inside Russia ahead of Trump-Putin-Xi summit
sources.text:
Germany and the U.K. have pushed back against U.S. criticism of Ukraine's deep strike campaign inside Russia, underscoring tensions between Washington and European allies over Kyiv's war strategy.
The clash comes ahead of a highly anticipated trilateral meeting on Thursday between U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China.
Geopolitical flashpoints such as trade, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons are expected to be a major focus of Trump, Putin and Xi's meeting, with external observers closely monitoring any discussion of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Speaking at NATO's headquarters in Belgium on Tuesday, U.S. Undersecretary of Defense Elbridge Colby likened Ukraine's deep strikes inside Russia to a spectacle, adding that they "have not been effective in driving an end to the war, nor do they contribute to blunting Russia's advances on the front line."
The Pentagon policy chief acknowledged Ukraine's mid-range strike campaign using novel drone technologies and tactics to deny Russian advances on the front line has proven "very effective."
He added that Ukraine's Armed Forces gained more territory than Russia for the second consecutive month in October.
However, Colby said Ukraine's deep strikes targeting "civilian infrastructure," citing Russia's biggest online retailer Wildberries, "have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate."
Kyiv has said that warehouses targeted by Ukrainian drones were involved in providing Russian forces with drone components, navigation equipment and other military components. Wildberries and the Kremlin have denied the company is involved in Russia's war in Ukraine.
Asked whether he shared Colby's position on Ukraine's deep strike campaign inside Russia, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said criticizing strikes designed to destroy strategic military and military-use targets in Russia "is quite a stupid thing, I think."
"Instead of criticizing that, we should rather criticize and talk about the terroristic strikes every night and every day on civil energy, water and heating infrastructure in Ukraine. This is kind of terrorism," Pistorius said at a news conference.
British Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting echoed those comments, saying it is "not for us to tell Ukraine how to fight their war."
He added: "There is no doubt in my mind that it has helped to degrade Putin's war machine, buying time and saving lives."
Kerch Bridge
Trump has previously called on Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries and infrastructure used to produce and distribute diesel, saying the attacks were responsible for a global shortage.
Ukraine has stepped up its strikes on Russian oil facilities and logistics infrastructure in recent months, seeking to raise the cost of the war for Moscow after more than 4½ years of conflict.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday lauded an "unprecedented operation" targeting the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea in what marked a symbolic blow to the Kremlin's war effort.
A coordinated drone and missile strike on the bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian forces and is one of Putin's signature projects, damaged the crossing.
In response, Russia said the bridge would be restored and "will be even better than before."

main.title: EU proposes new €45 billion Ukraine loan to be repaid by Russia
main.summary: European Commission President Ursula von ⁠der Leyen announced on Wednesday a proposed €45 billion loan to Ukraine for 2027 to help cover around two-thirds ​of Kyiv's financing ​needs. The loan will be repaid ⁠through future ⁠war reparations by Russia, von der Leyen added.
